title: Netflix Treats GPU Reliability as a Distributed Systems Problem
gist: Netflix describes a Kubernetes-based GPU reliability platform with layered fail-closed health checks, graduated automated remediation and checkpointed elastic training, reporting >99.95% GPU-node availability and job success up from ~98% to >99.5%.

insights.claim: Standard cloud VM health checks do not show that a GPU can run distributed training: Netflix found GPUs that answer status queries yet fail once memory is allocated or sustained compute begins.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Plain instance health is a poor proxy for AI capacity; usable-GPU availability needs deeper probes.

insights.claim: A network adapter can be present with fewer links than expected, letting collective operations run at severely reduced bandwidth without an outright failure.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Partial degradation, not hard failure, is a hidden throughput tax on large training runs.

insights.claim: Netflix's checks are fail-closed: a hung diagnostic times out and marks the machine unhealthy, with kernel-log fallback paths if the normal GPU diagnostic mechanism fails.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Fail-closed design is a reusable pattern for fleet health in expensive accelerator clusters.
insights.quote: If a diagnostic tool hangs, its timeout marks the machine unhealthy rather than allowing a broken check to report success.
insights.locator: The checks are deliberately designed to fail closed

insights.claim: Netflix escalates remediation progressively, from blocking new work to draining, job kills, GPU resets, reboots or replacement, integrated with Karpenter node auto-repair plus policies on tolerance time and disruption budget.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Graduated response preserves scarce GPU capacity versus replacing whole machines on first fault.
insights.locator: Detecting a fault is only half the problem

insights.claim: Netflix reports more than 99.95% GPU-node availability and job success rising from about 98% to more than 99.5%.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Concrete benchmark for GPU fleet reliability; each point of job success matters for multi-week runs.
insights.locator: The approach has produced measurable results

insights.claim: Large AI training runs lock workers in lockstep for weeks across hundreds of GPUs, so one failed GPU, degraded NIC or slow machine can halt or slow the whole job.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Reliability scales inversely with cluster size, raising the value of fault-tolerance tooling.

insights.claim: Netflix makes hardware failure cheaper rather than eliminating it, using checkpointing, elastic workers and automatic retries while classifying application failures separately to avoid restarting software bugs.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Recovery cost, not failure rate, is the lever for training goodput.
insights.locator: Large jobs use checkpointing and elastic workers

insights.claim: Netflix treats the training job as a distributed system and identifies a single slow rank holding back a synchronous job, since a GPU need not fail to reduce throughput.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Stragglers are an under-monitored throughput drain in synchronous training.
insights.locator: Netflix also treats the training job itself

insights.claim: Netflix uses MIG to let small inference workloads share GPUs with memory-level isolation and is moving toward Kubernetes Dynamic Resource Allocation for topology-aware placement.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Fractional GPU sharing improves inference utilisation economics.
insights.locator: Netflix is also using NVIDIA's Multi-Instance GPU

insights.claim: Meta reports hardware failures caused more than 66% of training interruptions in its Llama 3 experience, and invests in detecting silent data corruption at cluster scale.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Corroborates that hardware faults dominate large-run interruptions.
insights.locator: Meta also uses extensive hardware diagnostics

insights.claim: At thousands of GPUs, reliability can no longer be treated as simply keeping individual machines available; it requires validating before scheduling, monitoring during execution, and measuring goodput.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Goodput-focused operations tooling is a growing layer of the AI infra stack.
insights.locator: Both approaches reflect the same underlying reality
